get.bucket: A bucket. Fill it at the water.
get.bucketSand: Beach sand. Take it to Thea's furnace.
get.knife: A mushroom knife. The brush cleans.
get.dyeBundle: The four flowers. Take them to the table.
get.splitWood: The branch, in two. Take it to the dirt.
get.stool: A stool. It does nothing. It looks nice.
get.lantern: A lantern. It lights up when it gets dark.
get.flowerPot: A stone pot. The flower follows the season.
get.sundial: A sundial. The shadow tells the hour.
get.windChime: A wind chime. It rings when the wind blows.

cut.aimKeys: Z when the blade is between the marks
cut.aimTouch: Tap when the blade is between the marks
cut.sawTouch: Swipe side to side to saw
cut.tooHigh: Too high. Cut close to the ground.
cut.tooHighVolva: Too high. Keep the cup at the base.
cut.tooDeep: Too deep. That tears the mycelium.
cut.mycelium: Those white threads are the fungus itself: the mycelium. Left in the soil, it fruits again.

clean.title: Clean
clean.why: Brush, don't wash: mushrooms soak up water.

puffball.curiosity: Rain does the work: every drop that hits it puffs out spores.
puffball.cut: Cut under the ball, at the base.
puffball.clean: Brush off the soil and loose spines.
notes: Old ones puff out a cloud of spores.

inkCap.curiosity: Within hours it melts into black ink. People once wrote with it.
inkCap.cut: Cut low on the slim stem. It's hollow.
inkCap.clean: Be quick: once picked, it turns to ink within hours.
notes: It melts into black ink full of spores.
Pick it young. It inks within hours.

morel.curiosity: It favors dying elms and old apple orchards.
morel.cut: Cut at the base. The whole thing is hollow.
morel.clean: Grit hides in the pits. Brush each one.
notes: Spores grow in tiny sacs, not gills.

chanterelle.curiosity: It smells of apricots, and hardly any bug will eat it.
chanterelle.cut: Cut at the base, just above the moss.
chanterelle.clean: Dirt hides in the ridges. Brush them out.

flyAgaric.curiosity: It was once crumbled into milk to kill flies. Hence the name.
flyAgaric.cut: Cut below the soil line. The cup at the base, the volva, is how amanitas are told apart.
flyAgaric.clean: Brush gently: the white warts rub off.
notes: The warts are scraps of its egg-like veil.
The cup at the base marks an amanita.

porcini.curiosity: A single one can weigh over a kilo.
porcini.cut: Cut at the base of the thick stem.
porcini.clean: Brush the cap. White pores underneath mean it's young.

oyster.curiosity: It hunts: a drop of it stuns tiny worms, and it digests them.
oyster.cut: Cut the short stem, close to the bark.
oyster.clean: Brush out the leaf caught in the gills.
notes: Grows in shelves on dead wood, sideways.
Breaks the wood down and gives it back to the soil.

jackOLantern.curiosity: It glows in the dark: the gills light up a faint green.
jackOLantern.cut: Cut low, where the stems join.
jackOLantern.clean: Brush it, but never eat it.
notes: True gills, thin ones: the chanterelle has folds.
Looks like a chanterelle, but it's poison.

notebook.title: Field notebook
notebook.keys: Arrows turn the pages  ·  X close

entry.knife: A gift from Shui, with a brush on the handle. Cutting a mushroom instead of pulling it leaves whole what it has under the ground.
entry.axe: Marco's axe. It fells the dry tree and splits the stick on the chopping block.
entry.shovel: Sisi's shovel. It opens the holes in the cracked earth, where the dye seeds will live.
entry.bucket: A wooden bucket. Fill it with water; the water feeds what was planted and puts out fire.
entry.pickaxe: Thea's pickaxe. It breaks rock, and the rock gives stone, coal or ore, depending on the vein.
entry.scythe: The scythe Death left at the camp. It cuts tall grass. Death never came back for it.
entry.key: The key to the high garden. Whoever closes the valley's last request hands it over.
entry.wood: A stick from a dry tree. It becomes a bridge over water, stands up on Marco's block and, lit, becomes a torch.
entry.splitWood: The stick split in two on the block. Split wood dries faster and catches fire more easily.
entry.stone: A stone the pickaxe broke loose. In water it becomes a ford; on lava it cools into ground.
entry.charcoal: Coal, taken from the black vein by the lava. In the furnace it steals the oxygen from the ore and leaves the iron.
entry.ore: Iron ore: stone with iron trapped inside, as rust. On its own it is good for nothing.
entry.bloom: The iron bloom that comes out of the furnace: spongy iron, full of slag. It only becomes a bar by being hammered.
entry.iron: A real iron bar. From the ore to here: the coal, the furnace and the hammer.
entry.sand: Sand from the north beach, in a bucket, from a little mound the wind piled up. It is almost all silica, the stuff glass is made of.
entry.ash: Ash from a fire. It has potash, which helps the sand melt in a cooler fire.
entry.glass: Glass of sand and ash, melted in Thea's furnace. Polished, it becomes a lens.
entry.dyeSeeds: Sisi's mixed seeds: four plants that give dye. Each one goes in a hole.
entry.dyeBundle: The four dye flowers, picked. The colours of Sisi's painting come from them.
entry.brush: Sisi's brush. With it, the painting on the easel gets the colours of the flowers.
entry.telescope: Thea's telescope, with the glass lens. From the top of the plateau it brings the stars closer.
entry.stool: A twig stool, made at the camp workbench. It is just for looks.
entry.lantern: Twig and charcoal. It lights itself when dark falls, and rests by day.
entry.flowerPot: A stone pot with charcoal at the bottom: charcoal holds water and nutrients in the soil. The flower changes with the season.
entry.sundial: The twig's shadow moves with the sun and points to the hour. At night, with no sun, it tells nothing.
entry.cairn: Stones piled up, the biggest at the bottom. Piles like this have marked mountain trails for thousands of years.
entry.windChime: Shards of iron ore hung from a hook. They knock together when a gust goes by.

briansMansion.name: Brian's Mansion
briansMansion.text: A horror game in a haunted mansion, made in RPG Maker by a boy, for kids: the first dream of making games. It never came out on a cartridge; this is the cartridge he dreamed of.

zeroToOne.name: Zero To One
zeroToOne.text: Zero is a programmer stuck in a pointless routine. In five days he drops everything and leaves: from zero to one. In the game, everything alive is blue.

tinyRpgStudio.name: Tiny RPG Studio
tinyRpgStudio.text: A web game engine with a big community: more than 60 games made and shared with it. In 2026 came the first Tiny RPG Jam, with 17 entries.

diploma.name: Computer Science diploma
diploma.text: The science of what can be computed, and how: algorithms, data, languages and machines. It began on paper, with Ada Lovelace and Alan Turing, before computers existed: the machine is just the fastest way to do the sum.

journey.name: Journey
journey.text: A robed traveller crosses the desert toward the light on top of the mountain. No one speaks: whoever you meet on the way has no name and talks by singing. This is where games started to be thought of as art.

goneHome.name: Gone Home
goneHome.text: A stormy night in 1995: a daughter comes home from abroad to an empty house; in the letters and drawers, her sister's story. The walking sim that got famous: it showed games can go beyond action and combat and move you.

discoElysium.name: Disco Elysium
discoElysium.text: A detective wakes up in a hostel without remembering his own name, with a hanged man in the yard to investigate. No combat: his skills are voices arguing inside his head.
notes: Over a million words: a game you read like a novel.

book1984.text: Winston rewrites the past at the Ministry of Truth, under Big Brother's eyes. Newspeak shrinks the words until there is no way left to think against the Party.
notes: Freedom is being able to say that two and two make four.

odyssey2001.name: 2001: A Space Odyssey
odyssey2001.text: From apes facing the monolith to a ship bound for Jupiter, with HAL 9000, the computer that refuses to open the door. This is where the astronaut's missions in this valley came from.

bookClub.name: The club's bookmark
bookClub.text: Everyone reads the same technical or science book at home, and then the group talks it over. The mountains in the drawing are the ones in the name.

nomadPostcard.name: Postcard from the coast
nomadPostcard.text: A whole year of moving, one state at a time, up the coast of Brazil: the sea, the sand, the palm trees, and the work fitting in a backpack.

meditation.title: Meditation
facts: The mind wanders almost half of our waking time: 47%, in a study of 2,250 people. Meditating is not stopping that; it is noticing when it happens.
The exercise is the return: the mind drifts off, you notice, and you bring attention back. Each return is a repetition, like a lifted weight.
Breathing slowly, about six times a minute, lets the heartbeat vary more with the breath: a sign of the vagus nerve, the heart's brake, at work.
Putting a name to an emotion ("anger", "fear") lowers the response of the amygdala, the brain's alarm. That is why, here, each thought gets a name.
Meditation is usually safe, but some people feel discomfort. If it feels bad, stop. And meditation does not replace treatment.
There are two classic ways to meditate: focusing on one thing, like the breath, or watching whatever comes without holding on. Here you practise the first.
Breathing in, the heart speeds up a little; breathing out, it slows down. It is called respiratory sinus arrhythmia, and it is a sign of health.
Thirteen minutes a day for eight weeks improved attention, memory and mood in people who had never meditated. At four weeks, not yet.
In 47 studies with 3,515 people, mindfulness programmes eased anxiety, depression and pain modestly, without beating other treatments.
In people who have meditated for years, the brain network that pulls the mind away, the default mode network, is quieter during practice.
In a Stanford study, five minutes a day of sighs with a long exhale improved mood more than five minutes of meditation.
In people who had depression more than once, eight weeks of mindfulness-based therapy lowered relapse over a little more than a year from 49% to 38%.
For the heart, meditation may help as a complement, but the data are still modest.
An eight-week course did not change the brain structure of 218 people on MRI scans. Not everything said about meditation has been confirmed.
sources: Lehrer and Gevirtz, Frontiers in Psychology, 2014
Goldberg, Britton et al., Psychotherapy Research, 2021
Lutz et al., Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2008
Basso et al., Behavioural Brain Research, 2019
Goyal et al., JAMA Internal Medicine, 2014
Balban et al., Cell Reports Medicine, 2023
Levine et al., American Heart Association, 2017

squirrel.name: Red squirrel
squirrel.fact: It buries nuts and seeds for the winter and forgets many of them. The forgotten ones grow into trees.

bird.name: European robin
bird.fact: It follows whoever turns the soil, waiting for the worms that come up.

hare.name: European hare
hare.fact: It is born with its eyes open and already furry, ready to run.

frog.name: Iberian green frog
frog.fact: It also breathes through its skin, so it lives near water: the skin has to stay moist.

dragonfly.name: Emperor dragonfly
dragonfly.fact: It hunts in mid-air: it folds its legs into a basket and scoops up mosquitoes on the wing.

koi.name: Koi
koi.fact: It lives for decades, and learns who brings food: it comes to the edge when someone stops there.

cat.name: Black cat
cat.fact: It sleeps twelve to sixteen hours a day. This one chose the barrel.

ending.epigraph: Maybe life isn't about big things or some meaning behind it all, but about *small things*.
ending.afterword: The main adventure is over, but you can keep exploring and doing the side activities.

moon.name: The Moon
moon.seen: Each bright spot is a crater. The dark ones are seas of old lava.
moon.fact: Its light takes 1.3 seconds to get here.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.seen: Four little dots in a row beside it. They are moons.
jupiter.fact: Galileo saw them in 1610: not everything circles the Earth.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.seen: The rings are not one piece.
saturn.fact: They are billions of bits of ice and rock, each on its own orbit.

pleiades.name: The Pleiades
pleiades.seen: To the naked eye, a smudge. Through the lens, dozens of stars.
pleiades.fact: That light left there some 440 years ago.
